slot.brief: Two statements with overlapping categories; evaluate three conclusions including a possibility case and an either-or pair.

stem:
**Statements:**
Some sculptors are designers.
All designers are imaginative.

**Conclusions:**
I. Some sculptors being architects is a possibility.
II. Some sculptors are architects.
III. No sculptor is an architect.
options: Either conclusion II or III follows, but conclusion I does not follow
Conclusion I and either conclusion II or III follow
Neither conclusion I nor the either-or pair follows

verdicts.working: Some sculptors exist. Their relation to architects is unspecified, so overlap is possible (I). Conclusions II and III are contradictories; with sculptors known to exist, one must hold. Thus I and the either-or pair follow.

working:
I is possible: no statement rules out sculptors being architects.
II and III are each uncertain, but together they cover the alternatives; some sculptors exist.
A omits the either-or pair; B omits I; D denies both results.

Independent check: Some sculptors exist. Their relation to architects is unspecified, so overlap is possible (I). Conclusions II and III are contradictories; with sculptors known to exist, one must hold. Thus I and the either-or pair follow.
solution:
Some sculptors exist, and nothing restricts their relation to architects; hence some sculptors being architects is possible (I).
Conclusions II and III are contradictories, so one of them must hold.
Therefore, conclusion I and the either-or pair of conclusions II and III follow.
